name: The Sky-Face Vision (Palmer Eldritch face in the sky)
date_basis: Exegesis retrospect; Sutin Divine Invasions p.~117
summary: Driving in Marin County, PKD reports seeing a vast metal-and-jeweled face in the sky which he later called the face of Palmer Eldritch — sinister, mechanical, divine.
description: PKD reports that while driving in Marin County in early 1963 he saw, projected onto the sky, a massive face — metallic, jeweled, with a slot mouth and steel teeth — which he interpreted later as the face of evil divinity. He recounts the experience repeatedly across the Exegesis as the seed of *The Three Stigmata of Palmer Eldritch* (1965). The description varies: in some retellings the face is sinister-divine, in others it is the Antichrist, in others it is a Jungian shadow archetype.

pkd_interpretations.source: letters around composition of Palmer Eldritch
pkd_interpretations.interpretation: I saw the face of an evil god — what Christianity calls the Antichrist or Satan, but more accurately a sinister cosmic presence which I subsequently embodied as Palmer Eldritch.
The 1963 sky-face was the same intelligence that addressed me in 2-3-74 but in its negative polarity — the Black Iron Prison face of what would later show me itself as Zebra.
Horselover Fat in VALIS reports the same face — fictionalization confirms the experience as durable across decades.

scholar_interpretations.interpretation: Sutin reads this as the foundational visionary moment of PKD's career — the first event he could not subsequently explain away — and the proximate seed of *Three Stigmata* (1965).
Arnold suggests the 1963 vision is a late-onset hallucination of the kind reported in temporal-lobe epilepsy — clinically legible, not theological.
Peake takes the vision at something near face value, reading it as evidence of the kind of anomalous cognitive event he documents in *Is There Life After Death?*.

primary_sources.excerpt: *The Three Stigmata of Palmer Eldritch* (1965) is the literary record of this experience.
Multiple Exegesis segments 1974-1981 return to the 1963 face vision.

primary_quote: I can date my initial experience with the deity in the 'Palmer Eldritch' vision I had — saw in the sky — in the early sixties.
related_works: The Three Stigmata of Palmer Eldritch
contradiction_zone: yes — Sutin treats it as proto-mystical, Arnold as TLE, Peake as veridical anomalous cognition
pkd_doubt_evidence: PKD writes in 1979 letters that he cannot rule out a flashback or amphetamine effect for the 1963 experience.
